name: Hospital Green
lede: Hospital Green is a very light, slightly yellowish green from the 2010 xkcd color survey, named for an association with hospital walls and scrubs that our data does not trace further.

sections.title: A plain association, an undocumented coinage
sections.body:
The xkcd color survey is the only source we hold for this name, and its log records only the winning label for each swatch, not who wrote it first or exactly why [1]. The association with hospitals is plain enough on its own, since pale greens were a common choice for hospital walls and scrub uniforms through the twentieth century [1]. We hold no book or dated source tying this particular survey swatch to that history, so we do not claim one [1].

ISCC-NBS 1955 would file the swatch as a very light yellowish green, and the nearest library neighbors are [[mint|Mint]] and [[seafoam|Seafoam]], both similarly pale [2]. It reads as a [[green|green]] drained almost to a tint, closer to a pastel than to any clinical paint [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, holds no painting where this exact pale green covers five percent or more of the canvas [3]. A tint this light and this saturated sits outside the range that aged oil paint and varnish typically produce [3]. A match would be a computed color comparison, never a pigment identification [3].

origin.named_after: undocumented; a plain association with hospital walls and scrubs, unconfirmed

questions.q: Does our data confirm why hospital walls were historically painted pale green?
Where does our only source for the name Hospital Green come from?

openers: Hospital Green is pale enough that our archive of over 23,000 paintings finds no match for it at all.
